To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the thioureau-oxalic acid molten solvothermal synthesis method was used to successfully prepare CuFe(1- x)Cr(x) S2 (x ≤0.4) with high photocatalytic activities for the reduction of NO3 - ions in aqueous solutions.
a co-molten thiourea- oxalic acid solvothermal method has been developed to successfully incorporate Cr3+ in CuFe1-xCrxS2 (0≤x≤0.4) with chalcopyrite structure.

the thiouera-oxalic acid method can successfully synthesize Cr(3+) doped chalcopyrite sulfides, and that the CuFe(0.6)Cr(0.4)S2 sample exhibits the best photocatalytic activity toward the reduction of NO3- ions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a novel method of synthesis of CuFe(3+)(1-x)Cr(3+)(x)S2 (CuFe(1-x),Cr(x)S) solid solutions with high photocatalytic activities for the reduction of nitrates in aqueous solution.
the development of a novel synthetic route for preparing Fe(3+), Cr(3+) sulfide solid solutions, and the photocatalytic properties of the synthesized samples are investigated.
the development of a novel synthetic method for synthesizing CuFe(1- x)Cr(x) S2, and it provides a promising approach to synthesize other sulfide systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the co-molten approach is a powerful method to obtain chalcopyrite sulfides with a high concentration of Cr(3+).
the thiourear-oxalic acid solvothermal method is an effective method to synthesize Fe3+-Cr3+ sulfides.
the thioureas are effective in the synthesis of CuFe(3+)Cr(3+)S(2).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the co-molten system can be a promising method for the synthesis of sulfides with MS4 tetradahedral coordination.

the Cr(3+)-doped sulfides with tetrahedral coordination can be obtained by a co-molten thiourea-organic acid solvothermal method, which is of great importance for photocatalysis and other applications.
the thiourear-oxalic acid solvothermal method can be used as an effective way to prepare Fe(3+), Cr(3+) and Fe(3+)+Cr(3+) doped sulfide materials.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Cr(3+) can be incorporated into chalcopyrite to improve photocatalytic performance, which is very important for the application of CuFe(2)S4-based photocatalysts in the future.
the co-molten thiourea- oxalic acid method may be an efficient way to obtain sulfides containing Cr(3+).
